subsection.name: Introduction
subsection.p: A simple multiview map provider based on plugin-leaflet.

subsection.name: Configuration
subsection.p:
Add this module to your site:
<dependency> <groupId>fr.paris.lutece.plugins</groupId> <artifactId>module-forms-multiviewmapleaflet</artifactId> <version>[2.0.0]</version> <type>lutece-plugin</type> </dependency>

Then name this module's provider in the site configuration: plugin-forms reads the property forms.mapProvider.beanName.list and selects the CDI bean by name. forms.mapProvider.beanName.list=forms-multiviewmapleaflet.mapProvider

subsection.name: Tile source
subsection.p: The map draws on OpenStreetMap tiles by default. Point it somewhere else - a corporate proxy, the Geoplateforme, a self-hosted tile server - with two properties. forms-multiviewmapleaflet.tile.url=https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png forms-multiviewmapleaflet.tile.attribution=Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors

subsection.name: The tile server has to answer CORS
subsection.p: The back office is served with Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp, which refuses a cross-origin image fetched without CORS unless it carries a Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy header - tile servers don't. The module therefore fetches its tiles in CORS mode (crossorigin="anonymous"); OpenStreetMap answers Access-Control-Allow-Origin. A tile server without CORS needs, on the same screen, a configuration item on the Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy header as well (credentialless, or none).

subsection.name: Allow the tile host in the back-office Content-Security-Policy
subsection.p: Without this step the map draws grey: Leaflet builds the map and places the markers, but every tile is refused. The back-office policy ships with img-src 'self' data: blob: and a few Google hosts, and no tile server. The host configured above has to be allowed.

Do it for the multiview screen only rather than for the whole back office. In Systeme > Gestion des en-tetes de securite, open the Content-Security-Policy header and add a configuration item whose url pattern is /jsp/admin/plugins/forms/MultiviewForms.jsp** and whose custom value is the site's current policy with the tile host added to its img-src directive. The pattern is matched Ant-style against the servlet path plus the query string, and the custom value replaces the whole header on the screens that match.

A <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"> in a template does not work here: policies delivered by different mechanisms are enforced conjunctively (CSP Level 3, section 8.1), so a second policy can only restrict what the header already allows, never widen it.

subsection.name: Usage
subsection.p: The leaflet map will show on the multiview page if this module is enabled and there is a geolocation column.
